   526→def phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   527→    results = []
   528→    graph = deps_detector_mod.build_dep_graph(path)
   529→    lang.dep_graph = graph
   530→    zm = lang.zone_map
   531→
   532→    # Single-use (shared helper)
   533→    single_entries, single_candidates = (
   534→        single_use_detector_mod.detect_single_use_abstractions(
   535→            path, graph, barrel_names=lang.barrel_names
   536→        )
   537→    )
   538→    single_entries = filter_entries(zm, single_entries, "single_use")
   539→    results.extend(
   540→        make_single_use_issues(
   541→            single_entries, lang.get_area, skip_dir_names={"commands"}, stderr_fn=log
   542→        )
   543→    )
   544→    src_path = get_src_path()
   545→    shared_prefix = f"{src_path}/shared/"
   546→    tools_prefix = f"{src_path}/tools/"
   547→    coupling_entries, coupling_edge_counts = coupling_detector_mod.detect_coupling_violations(
   548→        path, graph, shared_prefix=shared_prefix, tools_prefix=tools_prefix
   549→    )
   550→    coupling_entries = filter_entries(zm, coupling_entries, "coupling")
   551→    _append_coupling_violations(results, coupling_entries)
   552→
   553→    # TS-specific: boundary candidates (deduplicated against single-use)
   554→    boundary_issues, _ = _make_boundary_issues(
   555→        single_entries, path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
   556→    )
   557→    results.extend(boundary_issues)
   558→
   559→    # TS-specific: cross-tool imports
   560→    cross_tool, cross_edge_counts = coupling_detector_mod.detect_cross_tool_imports(
   561→        path, graph, tools_prefix=tools_prefix
   562→    )
   563→    cross_tool = filter_entries(zm, cross_tool, "coupling")
   564→    _append_cross_tool_issues(results, cross_tool)
   565→
   566→    # Cycles + orphaned (shared helpers)
   567→    cycle_entries, _ = graph_detector_mod.detect_cycles(graph)
   568→    cycle_entries = filter_entries(zm, cycle_entries, "cycles", file_key="files")
   569→    results.extend(make_cycle_issues(cycle_entries, log))
   570→    orphan_entries, total_graph_files = orphaned_detector_mod.detect_orphaned_files(
   571→        path,
   572→        graph,
   573→        extensions=lang.extensions,
   574→        options=orphaned_detector_mod.OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   575→            extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   576→            extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   577→            dynamic_import_finder=deps_detector_mod.build_dynamic_import_targets,
   578→            alias_resolver=deps_detector_mod.ts_alias_resolver,
   579→        ),
   580→    )
   581→    orphan_entries = filter_entries(zm, orphan_entries, "orphaned")
   582→    results.extend(make_orphaned_issues(orphan_entries, log))
   583→
   584→    # Re-export facades (shared detector)
   585→    facade_entries, _ = facade_detector_mod.detect_reexport_facades(graph)
   586→    facade_entries = filter_entries(zm, facade_entries, "facade")
   587→    results.extend(make_facade_issues(facade_entries, log))
   588→
   589→    # TS-specific: pattern consistency
   590→    pattern_result = patterns_detector_mod.detect_pattern_anomalies_result(path)
   591→    pattern_entries = pattern_result.entries
   592→    total_areas = pattern_result.population_size
   593→    _append_pattern_issues(results, pattern_entries)
   594→
   595→    # TS-specific: naming consistency
   596→    naming_entries, total_dirs = naming_detector_mod.detect_naming_inconsistencies(
   597→        path,
   598→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   599→        skip_names=TS_SKIP_NAMES,
   600→        skip_dirs=TS_SKIP_DIRS,
   601→    )
   602→    _append_naming_issues(results, naming_entries)
   603→    log(f"         → {len(results)} coupling/structural issues total")
   604→    coupling_edges = coupling_edge_counts.eligible_edges
   605→    cross_edges = cross_edge_counts.eligible_edges
   606→    potentials = {
   607→        "single_use": adjust_potential(zm, single_candidates),
   608→        "coupling": coupling_edges + cross_edges,
   609→        "cycles": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   610→        "orphaned": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   611→        "patterns": total_areas,
   612→        "naming": total_dirs,
   613→        "facade": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   614→    }
   615→    return results, potentials
   616→

   618→def phase_smells(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   619→    smell_entries, total_smell_files = smells_detector_mod.detect_smells(path)
   620→    results = make_smell_issues(smell_entries, log)
   621→
   622→    # TS-specific: React state sync anti-patterns
   623→    react_entries, total_effects = react_detector_mod.detect_state_sync(path)
   624→    for e in react_entries:
   625→        setter_str = ", ".join(e["setters"])
   626→        results.append(
   627→            make_issue(
   628→                "react",
   629→                e["file"],
   630→                setter_str,
   631→                tier=3,
   632→                confidence="medium",
   633→                summary=f"State sync anti-pattern: useEffect only calls {setter_str}",
   634→                detail={"line": e["line"], "setters": e["setters"]},
   635→            )
   636→        )
   637→    if react_entries:
   638→        log(f"         react: {len(react_entries)} state sync anti-patterns")
   639→
   640→    # TS-specific: Context provider nesting depth
   641→    nesting_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_context_nesting(path)
   642→    for e in nesting_entries:
   643→        providers_str = " → ".join(e["providers"][:5])
   644→        results.append(
   645→            make_issue(
   646→                "react",
   647→                e["file"],
   648→                f"nesting::{e['depth']}",
   649→                tier=3,
   650→                confidence="medium",
   651→                summary=f"Deep provider nesting ({e['depth']} levels): {providers_str}",
   652→                detail={"depth": e["depth"], "providers": e["providers"]},
   653→            )
   654→        )
   655→    if nesting_entries:
   656→        log(f"         react: {len(nesting_entries)} deep provider nesting")
   657→
   658→    # TS-specific: Hook return bloat
   659→    hook_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_hook_return_bloat(path)
   660→    for e in hook_entries:
   661→        results.append(
   662→            make_issue(
   663→                "react",
   664→                e["file"],
   665→                f"hook_bloat::{e['hook']}",
   666→                tier=3,
   667→                confidence="medium",
   668→                summary=f"Hook return bloat: {e['hook']} returns {e['field_count']} fields",
   669→                detail={
   670→                    "hook": e["hook"],
   671→                    "field_count": e["field_count"],
   672→                    "line": e["line"],
   673→                },
   674→            )
   675→        )
   676→    if hook_entries:
   677→        log(f"         react: {len(hook_entries)} bloated hook returns")
   678→
   679→    # TS-specific: Boolean state explosion
   680→    bool_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_boolean_state_explosion(path)
   681→    for e in bool_entries:
   682→        states_str = ", ".join(e["states"][:5])
   683→        results.append(
   684→            make_issue(
   685→                "react",
   686→                e["file"],
   687→                f"bool_state::{e['prefix']}",
   688→                tier=3,
   689→                confidence="low",
   690→                summary=f"Boolean state explosion: {e['count']} boolean useState hooks ({states_str})",
   691→                detail={
   692→                    "count": e["count"],
   693→                    "setters": e["setters"],
   694→                    "states": e["states"],
   695→                    "line": e["line"],
   696→                },
   697→            )
   698→        )
   699→    if bool_entries:
   700→        log(f"         react: {len(bool_entries)} boolean state explosions")
   701→
   702→    return results, {
   703→        "smells": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_smell_files),
   704→        "react": total_effects,
   705→    }

    24→def _state_file_for_runtime(runtime) -> Path:
    25→    """Resolve the effective state file path for a command runtime."""
    26→    state_file = runtime.state_path
    27→    if isinstance(state_file, Path):
    28→        return state_file
    29→    return state_mod.STATE_FILE
    30→
    31→
    32→def _prune_excluded_issues(state: dict, pattern: str) -> list[str]:
    33→    """Drop issues whose file path matches a new exclusion pattern."""
    34→    issues = state.get("issues")
    35→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
    36→        return []
    37→
    38→    removed_ids = [
    39→        issue_id
    40→        for issue_id, issue in issues.items()
    41→        if isinstance(issue, dict)
    42→        and matches_exclusion(str(issue.get("file", "")), pattern)
    43→    ]
    44→    for issue_id in removed_ids:
    45→        issues.pop(issue_id, None)
    46→    return removed_ids
    47→
    48→
    49→def _purge_removed_ids_from_plan(state_file: Path, removed_ids: list[str]) -> int:
    50→    """Remove pruned issue IDs from queue/skips/clusters in plan.json."""
    51→    if not removed_ids:
    52→        return 0
    53→    plan_file = plan_path_for_state(state_file)
    54→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
    55→    purged = purge_ids(plan, removed_ids)
    56→    if purged:
    57→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
    58→    return purged
    59→
    60→
    61→def cmd_exclude(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    62→    """Add a path pattern to the exclude list and clean cached queue/state."""
    63→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    64→    config = runtime.config
    65→    state = runtime.state
    66→    state_file = _state_file_for_runtime(runtime)
    67→
    68→    config_mod.add_exclude_pattern(config, args.pattern)
    69→    config["needs_rescan"] = True
    70→    try:
    71→        config_mod.save_config(config)
    72→    except OSError as exc:
    73→        raise CommandError(f"could not save config: {exc}") from exc
    74→
    75→    removed_ids: list[str] = []
    76→    plan_purged = 0
    77→    if state_file.exists():
    78→        removed_ids = _prune_excluded_issues(state, args.pattern)
    79→        if removed_ids:
    80→            try:
    81→                state_mod.save_state(state, state_file)
    82→            except OSError as exc:
    83→                raise CommandError(f"could not save state: {exc}") from exc
    84→
    85→            try:
    86→                plan_purged = _purge_removed_ids_from_plan(state_file, removed_ids)
    87→            except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    88→                print(
    89→                    colorize("  Warning: could not update living plan.", "yellow"),
    90→                    file=sys.stderr,
    91→                )
    92→
    93→    print(colorize(f"Added exclude pattern: {args.pattern}", "green"))
    94→    if removed_ids:
    95→        print(f"  Removed {len(removed_ids)} matching issues from state.")
    96→        if plan_purged:
    97→            print(
    98→                colorize(
    99→                    f"  Plan updated: {plan_purged} item(s) removed from queue.",
   100→                    "dim",
   101→                )
   102→            )
   103→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
   104→    if config_warning:
   105→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
   106→
   107→
   108→__all__ = ["cmd_exclude"]
   109→

    11→)

    25→import desloppify.intelligence.narrative.core as narrative_mod
    26→
    27→
    28→def cmd_suppress(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    29→    """Suppress issues matching a pattern."""
    30→    attestation = getattr(args, "attest", None)
    31→    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
    32→        show_attestation_requirement("Suppress", attestation, ATTEST_EXAMPLE)
    33→        raise CommandError("Suppress requires a valid attestation.")
    34→
    35→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    36→    state_file = runtime.state_path
    37→    state = runtime.state
    38→    prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
    39→
    40→    config = runtime.config
    41→    config_mod.add_ignore_pattern(config, args.pattern)
    42→    config["needs_rescan"] = True
    43→    save_config_or_exit(config)
    44→
    45→    removed = state_mod.remove_ignored_issues(state, args.pattern)
    46→    state.setdefault("attestation_log", []).append(
    47→        {
    48→            "timestamp": state.get("last_scan"),
    49→            "command": "suppress",
    50→            "pattern": args.pattern,
    51→            "attestation": attestation,
    52→            "affected": removed,
    53→        }
    54→    )
    55→    save_state_or_exit(state, state_file)
    56→
    57→    print(colorize(f"Added suppress pattern: {args.pattern}", "green"))
    58→    if removed:
    59→        print(f"  Removed {removed} matching issues from state.")
    60→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
    61→    if config_warning:
    62→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
    63→    show_score_with_plan_context(state, prev)
    64→
    65→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
    66→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
    67→    narrative = narrative_mod.compute_narrative(
    68→        state,
    69→        context=narrative_mod.NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="suppress"),
    70→    )
    71→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
    72→    write_query(
    73→        {

    77→            "overall_score": scores.overall,

1→"""Developer utilities."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import ast
     7→import keyword
     8→import re
     9→
    10→from desloppify.app.commands.dev_scaffold_templates import build_scaffold_files
    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import safe_write_text
    12→from desloppify.base.exception_sets import CommandError
    13→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    14→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
    15→
    16→
    17→def cmd_dev(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    18→    """Dispatch developer subcommands."""
    19→    action = getattr(args, "dev_action", None)
    20→    if action == "scaffold-lang":
    21→        try:
    22→            _cmd_scaffold_lang(args)
    23→        except ValueError as ex:
    24→            raise CommandError(str(ex)) from ex
    25→        return
    26→    raise CommandError("Unknown dev action. Use `desloppify dev scaffold-lang`.")
    27→
    28→
    29→def _normalize_lang_name(raw: str) -> str:
    30→    name = raw.strip().lower().replace("-", "_")
    31→    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*", name):
    32→        raise ValueError("language name must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*")
    33→    if keyword.iskeyword(name):
    34→        raise ValueError(f"language name cannot be a Python keyword: {name}")
    35→    return name
    36→
    37→
    38→def _normalize_extensions(values: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    39→    out: list[str] = []
    40→    for val in values or []:
    41→        ext = val.strip()
    42→        if not ext:
    43→            continue
    44→        if not ext.startswith("."):
    45→            ext = "." + ext
    46→        if not re.fullmatch(r"\.[a-z0-9]+", ext):
    47→            raise ValueError(f"invalid extension: {val!r}")
    48→        out.append(ext)
    49→    if not out:
    50→        raise ValueError("at least one --extension is required")
    51→    seen: set[str] = set()
    52→    deduped: list[str] = []
    53→    for ext in out:
    54→        if ext not in seen:
    55→            seen.add(ext)
    56→            deduped.append(ext)
    57→    return deduped
    58→
    59→
    60→def _normalize_markers(values: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    61→    out: list[str] = []
    62→    for val in values or []:
    63→        marker = val.strip()
    64→        if marker and marker not in out:
    65→            out.append(marker)
    66→    return out
    67→
    68→
    69→def _class_name(lang_name: str) -> str:
    70→    return "".join(part.capitalize() for part in lang_name.split("_")) + "Config"
    71→
    72→
    73→def _template_files(
    74→    lang_name: str,
    75→    extensions: list[str],
    76→    markers: list[str],
    77→    default_src: str,
    78→) -> dict[str, str]:
    79→    class_name = _class_name(lang_name)
    80→    return build_scaffold_files(
    81→        lang_name=lang_name,
    82→        class_name=class_name,
    83→        extensions=extensions,
    84→        markers=markers,
    85→        default_src=default_src,
    86→    )
    87→
    88→
    89→def _render_array(items: list[str]) -> str:
    90→    return ", ".join(repr(x) for x in items)
    91→
    92→
    93→def _append_toml_array_item(text: str, key: str, value: str) -> str:
    94→    pattern = re.compile(
    95→        rf"(^\s*{re.escape(key)}\s*=\s*\[)(.*?)(\]\s*$)",
    96→        re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,
    97→    )
    98→    match = pattern.search(text)
    99→    if not match:
   100→        return text
   101→
   102→    raw = match.group(2).strip()
   103→    parsed = ast.literal_eval("[" + raw + "]") if raw else []
   104→    if not isinstance(parsed, list):
   105→        return text
   106→    if value in parsed:
   107→        return text
   108→
   109→    parsed.append(value)
   110→    replacement = f"{match.group(1)}{_render_array(parsed)}{match.group(3)}"
   111→    return text[: match.start()] + replacement + text[match.end() :]
   112→
   113→
   114→def _wire_pyproject(lang_name: str) -> bool:
   115→    pyproject_path = get_project_root() / "pyproject.toml"
   116→    if not pyproject_path.is_file():
   117→        return False
   118→
   119→    original = pyproject_path.read_text()
   120→    updated = original
   121→    updated = _append_toml_array_item(
   122→        updated,
   123→        "testpaths",
   124→        f"desloppify/languages/{lang_name}/tests",
   125→    )
   126→
   127→    if updated != original:
   128→        safe_write_text(pyproject_path, updated)
   129→        return True
   130→    return False
   131→
   132→
   133→def _cmd_scaffold_lang(args: object) -> None:
   134→    raw_name = getattr(args, "name", "")
   135→    lang_name = _normalize_lang_name(raw_name)
   136→    extensions = _normalize_extensions(getattr(args, "extension", None))
   137→    markers = _normalize_markers(getattr(args, "marker", None))
   138→    default_src = getattr(args, "default_src", "src") or "src"
   139→    force = bool(getattr(args, "force", False))
   140→    wire_pyproject = bool(getattr(args, "wire_pyproject", True))
   141→
   142→    lang_dir = get_project_root() / "desloppify" / "languages" / lang_name
   143→    if lang_dir.exists() and not force:
   144→        raise CommandError(
   145→            f"Language directory already exists: {lang_dir}. Use --force to overwrite."
   146→        )
   147→
   148→    files = _template_files(lang_name, extensions, markers, default_src)
   149→    for rel_path, content in files.items():
   150→        target = lang_dir / rel_path
   151→        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   152→        if target.exists() and not force:
   153→            continue
   154→        safe_write_text(target, content)
   155→
   156→    wired = _wire_pyproject(lang_name) if wire_pyproject else False
   157→
   158→    print(colorize(f"Scaffolded language plugin: {lang_name}", "green"))
   159→    print(f"  Path: {lang_dir}")
   160→    print(f"  Extensions: {', '.join(extensions)}")
   161→    print(f"  Markers: {', '.join(markers) if markers else '(none)'}")
   162→    print(f"  pyproject.toml updated: {'yes' if wired else 'no'}")
   163→    print(
   164→        colorize(
   165→            "  Next: implement real phases/commands/detectors and run pytest.", "dim"
   166→        )
   167→    )
   168→

1→"""langs command: list all available language plugins with depth and tools."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import logging
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     9→from desloppify.languages._framework import registry_state
    10→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangConfig
    11→from desloppify.languages._framework.discovery import load_all
    12→from desloppify.languages._framework.generic import SHARED_PHASE_LABELS
    13→from desloppify.languages._framework.resolution import make_lang_config
    14→
    15→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    16→
    17→_DEPTH_BARS = {
    18→    "full": 8,
    19→    "standard": 5,
    20→    "shallow": 3,
    21→    "minimal": 2,
    22→}
    23→
    24→_DEPTH_MAX = 8
    25→
    26→
    27→def _depth_bar(depth: str) -> str:
    28→    """Render a depth bar like ████░░░░."""
    29→    filled = _DEPTH_BARS.get(depth, 2)
    30→    empty = _DEPTH_MAX - filled
    31→    return "\u2588" * filled + "\u2591" * empty
    32→
    33→
    34→def _get_tool_labels(cfg: LangConfig) -> str:
    35→    """Extract tool labels from phases."""
    36→    if cfg.integration_depth == "full":
    37→        return "custom detectors"
    38→    labels = [p.label for p in cfg.phases if p.label not in SHARED_PHASE_LABELS]
    39→    suffix = " (auto-fix)" if cfg.fixers else ""
    40→    return (", ".join(labels) if labels else "none") + suffix
    41→
    42→
    43→def cmd_langs(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    44→    """List all available languages with depth and tool info."""
    45→    load_all()
    46→
    47→    configs: list[tuple[str, LangConfig]] = []
    48→    for name, obj in sorted(registry_state.all_items()):
    49→        if isinstance(obj, LangConfig):
    50→            configs.append((name, obj))
    51→        else:
    52→            try:
    53→                cfg = make_lang_config(name, obj)
    54→                configs.append((name, cfg))
    55→            except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError) as exc:
    56→                logger.debug("Skipping unresolvable lang config %s: %s", name, exc)
    57→                continue
    58→
    59→    # Sort: full first, then standard, shallow, minimal; alphabetical within
    60→    depth_order = {"full": 0, "standard": 1, "shallow": 2, "minimal": 3}
    61→    configs.sort(key=lambda x: (depth_order.get(x[1].integration_depth, 9), x[0]))
    62→
    63→    # Column widths
    64→    name_width = max(len(name) for name, _ in configs) + 2 if configs else 14
    65→    name_width = max(name_width, 14)
    66→
    67→    print()
    68→    header = f"{'Language':<{name_width}}{'Depth':<14}Tools"
    69→    print(colorize(header, "bold"))
    70→    print("\u2500" * 60)
    71→
    72→    for name, cfg in configs:
    73→        depth = getattr(cfg, "integration_depth", "full")
    74→        bar = _depth_bar(depth)
    75→        tools = _get_tool_labels(cfg)
    76→        print(f"{name:<{name_width}}{bar}    {tools}")
    77→    print()
    78→

    19→def cmd_zone(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    20→    """Handle zone subcommands: show, set, clear."""
    21→    action = getattr(args, "zone_action", None)
    22→    if action in (None, "show"):
    23→        _zone_show(args)
    24→    elif action == "set":
    25→        _zone_set(args)
    26→    elif action == "clear":
    27→        _zone_clear(args)
    28→    else:
    29→        raise CommandError("Usage: desloppify zone {show|set|clear}")
    30→
    31→
    32→def _zone_show(args):
    33→    """Show zone classifications for all scanned files."""
    34→    state_file = state_path(args)
    35→    if not state_file.exists():
    36→        raise CommandError("No state file found — run a scan first.")
    37→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
    38→    if not lang or not lang.file_finder:
    39→        raise CommandError("No language detected — run a scan first.")
    40→
    41→    path = Path(args.path)
    42→    overrides = command_runtime(args).config.get("zone_overrides", {})
    43→
    44→    files = lang.file_finder(path)
    45→    zone_map = FileZoneMap(
    46→        files, lang.zone_rules, rel_fn=rel, overrides=overrides or None
    47→    )
    48→
    49→    # Group files by zone
    50→    by_zone: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    51→    for f in sorted(files, key=lambda f: rel(f)):
    52→        zone = zone_map.get(f)
    53→        by_zone.setdefault(zone.value, []).append(f)
    54→
    55→    total = len(files)
    56→    print(colorize(f"\nZone classifications ({total} files)\n", "bold"))
    57→
    58→    for zone_val in ["production", "test", "config", "generated", "script", "vendor"]:
    59→        zone_files = by_zone.get(zone_val, [])
    60→        if not zone_files:
    61→            continue
    62→        print(colorize(f"  {zone_val} ({len(zone_files)} files)", "bold"))
    63→        for f in zone_files:
    64→            rp = rel(f)
    65→            is_override = rp in overrides
    66→            suffix = colorize(" (override)", "cyan") if is_override else ""
    67→            print(f"    {rp}{suffix}")
    68→        print()
    69→
    70→    if overrides:
    71→        print(colorize(f"  {len(overrides)} override(s) active", "dim"))
    72→    print(colorize("  Override: desloppify zone set <file> <zone>", "dim"))
    73→    print(colorize("  Clear:    desloppify zone clear <file>", "dim"))
    74→    print_agent_plan(
    75→        ["Fix misclassified files, then re-scan."],
    76→        next_command="desloppify scan",
    77→    )
    78→
    79→
    80→def _zone_set(args):
    81→    """Set a zone override for a file."""
    82→    filepath = args.zone_path
    83→    zone_value = args.zone_value
    84→
    85→    # Validate zone value
    86→    valid_zones = {z.value for z in Zone}
    87→    if zone_value not in valid_zones:
    88→        raise CommandError(
    89→            f"Invalid zone: {zone_value}. Valid: {', '.join(sorted(valid_zones))}"
    90→        )
    91→
    92→    normalized = rel(filepath)
    93→    config = command_runtime(args).config
    94→    config.setdefault("zone_overrides", {})[normalized] = zone_value
    95→    try:
    96→        config_mod.save_config(config)
    97→    except OSError as e:
    98→        raise CommandError(f"could not save config: {e}") from e
    99→    print(f"  Set {normalized} → {zone_value}")
   100→    print(colorize("  Run `desloppify scan` to apply.", "dim"))
   101→    print(colorize("  Next command: `desloppify scan`", "dim"))
   102→
   103→
   104→def _zone_clear(args):
   105→    """Clear a zone override for a file."""
   106→    filepath = args.zone_path
   107→
   108→    normalized = rel(filepath)
   109→    config = command_runtime(args).config
   110→    overrides = config.get("zone_overrides", {})

1→"""update-skill command: install or update the desloppify skill document."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import urllib.error
     7→import urllib.request
     8→
     9→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    10→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import safe_write_text
    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
    12→from desloppify.app.skill_docs import (
    13→    SKILL_BEGIN,
    14→    SKILL_END,
    15→    SKILL_TARGETS,
    16→    SKILL_VERSION,
    17→    SKILL_VERSION_RE,
    18→    SkillInstall,
    19→    find_installed_skill,
    20→)
    21→
    22→_RAW_BASE = (
    23→    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peteromallet/desloppify/main/docs"
    24→)
    25→
    26→
    27→def _download(filename: str) -> str:
    28→    """Download a file from the desloppify docs directory on GitHub."""
    29→    url = f"{_RAW_BASE}/{filename}"
    30→    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as resp:  # noqa: S310
    31→        return resp.read().decode("utf-8")
    32→
    33→
    34→def _build_section(skill_content: str, overlay_content: str | None) -> str:
    35→    """Assemble the complete skill section from downloaded parts."""
    36→    parts = [skill_content.rstrip()]
    37→    if overlay_content:
    38→        parts.append(overlay_content.rstrip())
    39→    return "\n\n".join(parts) + "\n"
    40→
    41→
    42→def _replace_section(file_content: str, new_section: str) -> str:
    43→    """Replace the desloppify section in a shared file, preserving surrounding content.
    44→
    45→    Uses first ``<!-- desloppify-begin -->`` and last ``<!-- desloppify-end -->``
    46→    so the overlay (which also has an end marker) is captured correctly.
    47→    """
    48→    begin = file_content.find(SKILL_BEGIN)
    49→    end = file_content.rfind(SKILL_END)
    50→    if begin == -1 or end == -1:
    51→        # No section markers — append (first install into existing shared file).
    52→        return file_content.rstrip() + "\n\n" + new_section
    53→
    54→    before = file_content[:begin]
    55→    after = file_content[end + len(SKILL_END):]
    56→    before = before.rstrip() + "\n\n" if before.strip() else ""
    57→    after = "\n" + after.lstrip("\n") if after.strip() else "\n"
    58→    return before + new_section + after
    59→
    60→
    61→def resolve_interface(
    62→    explicit: str | None = None,
    63→    install: SkillInstall | None = None,
    64→) -> str | None:
    65→    """Resolve which interface to update.
    66→
    67→    Uses the explicit argument if given, otherwise infers from an existing
    68→    install's overlay marker or file path.
    69→    """
    70→    if explicit:
    71→        return explicit.lower()
    72→
    73→    if install is None:
    74→        install = find_installed_skill()
    75→    if not install:
    76→        return None
    77→
    78→    if install.overlay:
    79→        return install.overlay.lower()
    80→
    81→    for name, (target, _overlay, _ded) in SKILL_TARGETS.items():
    82→        if target == install.rel_path:
    83→            return name
    84→    return None
    85→
    86→
    87→def update_installed_skill(interface: str) -> bool:
    88→    """Download and install the skill document for the given interface.
    89→
    90→    Returns True on success, False on failure. Prints status messages.
    91→    """
    92→    target_rel, overlay_name, dedicated = SKILL_TARGETS[interface]
    93→    target_path = get_project_root() / target_rel
    94→
    95→    print(colorize(f"Downloading skill document ({interface})...", "dim"))
    96→    try:
    97→        skill_content = _download("SKILL.md")
    98→        overlay_content = _download(f"{overlay_name}.md") if overlay_name else None
    99→    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError) as exc:
   100→        print(colorize(f"Download failed: {exc}", "red"))
   101→        return False
   102→
   103→    if "desloppify-skill-version" not in skill_content:
   104→        print(colorize("Downloaded content doesn't look like a skill document.", "red"))
   105→        return False
   106→
   107→    new_section = _build_section(skill_content, overlay_content)
   108→
   109→    target_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   110→    if dedicated:
   111→        result = new_section
   112→    elif target_path.is_file():
   113→        existing = target_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   114→        result = _replace_section(existing, new_section)
   115→    else:
   116→        result = new_section
   117→
   118→    safe_write_text(target_path, result)
   119→
   120→    version_match = SKILL_VERSION_RE.search(new_section)
   121→    version = version_match.group(1) if version_match else "?"
   122→    print(
   123→        colorize(
   124→            f"Updated {target_rel} (v{version}, tool expects v{SKILL_VERSION})",
   125→            "green",
   126→        )
   127→    )
   128→    return True
   129→
   130→
   131→def cmd_update_skill(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   132→    """Install or update the desloppify skill document."""
   133→    interface = resolve_interface(getattr(args, "interface", None))
   134→
   135→    if not interface:
   136→        print(colorize("No installed skill document found.", "yellow"))
   137→        print()
   138→        names = ", ".join(sorted(SKILL_TARGETS))
   139→        print(f"Install with: desloppify update-skill <{names}>")
   140→        return
   141→
   142→    if interface not in SKILL_TARGETS:
   143→        names = ", ".join(sorted(SKILL_TARGETS))
   144→        print(colorize(f"Unknown interface '{interface}'.", "red"))
   145→        print(f"Available: {names}")
   146→        return
   147→
   148→    update_installed_skill(interface)
   149→

     3→from __future__ import annotations

     8→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.lang import auto_detect_lang_name

    10→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root

    12→
    13→def _sole_existing_lang_state_file() -> Path | None:
    14→    """Return the only existing language-specific state file, if unambiguous."""
    15→    state_dir = get_project_root() / ".desloppify"
    16→    if not state_dir.exists():
    17→        return None
    18→    candidates = sorted(path for path in state_dir.glob("state-*.json") if path.is_file())
    19→    if len(candidates) == 1:
    20→        return candidates[0]
    21→    return None
    22→
    23→
    24→def _allow_lang_state_fallback(args: argparse.Namespace) -> bool:
    25→    """Whether command can safely fallback to the sole existing lang state file."""
    26→    # Scan should always honor detected/explicit language mapping to avoid cross-lang merges.
    27→    return getattr(args, "command", None) != "scan"
    28→
    29→
    30→def state_path(args: argparse.Namespace) -> Path | None:
    31→    """Get state file path from args, or None for default."""
    32→    path_arg = getattr(args, "state", None)

    43→        if fallback is not None:

    46→

    48→        fallback = _sole_existing_lang_state_file()
    49→        if fallback is not None:
    50→            return fallback
    51→    return None

    54→def require_completed_scan(state: dict) -> bool:

   147→def _line_security_issues(

   251→            line_issues.append(
   252→                _make_security_entry(

   256→                    check_id="unverified_jwt_decode",

   261→                )
   262→            )

   264→    return line_issues
   265→
   266→
   267→def _file_level_security_issues(
   268→    *,
   269→    filepath: str,
   270→    normalized_path: str,
   271→    lines: list[str],
   272→    content: str,
   273→) -> list[dict]:
   274→    """Detect file-level security patterns and return issues."""
   275→    file_issues: list[dict] = []
   276→
   277→    if _looks_like_edge_handler(normalized_path, content):
   278→        if not _handler_has_auth_check(content):
   279→            file_issues.append(
   280→                _make_security_entry(
   281→                    filepath,
   282→                    1,
   283→                    content.splitlines()[0] if lines else "",
   284→                    check_id="edge_function_missing_auth",
   285→                    summary="Edge function serves requests without authentication check",
   286→                    severity="high",
   287→                    confidence="medium",
   288→                    remediation="Add authentication check (e.g., authenticateRequest, auth.getUser)",
   289→                )
   290→            )
   291→
   292→    _check_json_parse_unguarded(filepath, lines, file_issues)
   293→    if filepath.endswith(".sql"):
   294→        _check_rls_bypass(filepath, content, lines, file_issues)
   295→    return file_issues
   296→
   297→
   298→def _looks_like_edge_handler(normalized_path: str, content: str) -> bool:
   299→    """Detect edge-function style handlers without relying on index.ts naming."""
   300→    in_edge_tree = "/functions/" in normalized_path.replace("\\", "/")
   301→    has_edge_entrypoint = bool(_SERVE_ASYNC_RE.search(content) or _EDGE_ENTRYPOINT_RE.search(content))
   302→    return in_edge_tree and has_edge_entrypoint
   303→
   304→
   305→def _extract_handler_body(content: str) -> str | None:
   306→    """Extract the body of the first serve() or exported handler function.
   307→
   308→    Uses brace-depth tracking to find the handler callback scope.
   309→    Returns the handler body text, or None if not found.
   310→    """
   311→    # Try serve(async (req) => { ... }) or serve(async function(req) { ... })
   312→    match = _SERVE_ASYNC_RE.search(content)
   313→    if not match:
   314→        match = _EDGE_ENTRYPOINT_RE.search(content)
   315→    if not match:
   316→        return None
   317→
   318→    # Find the first opening brace after the match
   319→    start = match.end()
   320→    brace_pos = content.find("{", start)
   321→    if brace_pos == -1:
   322→        return None
   323→
   324→    # Track brace depth to find the matching close brace
   325→    depth = 0
   326→    for i in range(brace_pos, len(content)):
   327→        ch = content[i]
   328→        if ch == "{":
   329→            depth += 1
   330→        elif ch == "}":
   331→            depth -= 1
   332→            if depth == 0:
   333→                return content[brace_pos : i + 1]
   334→    return None
   335→
   336→
   337→def _handler_has_auth_check(content: str) -> bool:
   338→    """Check if auth patterns exist inside the handler body, not just anywhere in the file."""
   339→    handler_body = _extract_handler_body(content)
   340→    if handler_body is None:
   341→        # Fallback to file-level check if we can't parse handler boundaries
   342→        return bool(_AUTH_CHECK_RE.search(content))
   343→    return bool(_AUTH_CHECK_RE.search(handler_body))
   344→
   345→
   346→def _is_in_try_scope(lines: list[str], target_line: int) -> bool:
   347→    """Check if target_line (1-indexed) is inside a try block by scanning backwards.
   348→
   349→    Tracks brace depth going upward. If we reach a `try` keyword when depth <= 0,
   350→    the target is inside a try block. Stops if we encounter a function/arrow boundary
   351→    (conservative: inner functions reset scope).
   352→    """
   353→    depth = 0
   354→    for i in range(target_line - 2, -1, -1):  # 0-indexed, go backwards
   355→        stripped = lines[i].strip()
   356→        # Stop at named function boundaries — inner functions are not guarded by outer try.
   357→        # Arrow functions (=>) are NOT a boundary: they may appear inside a try block.
   358→        if re.match(r"(?:async\s+)?function\b", stripped):
   359→            return False
   360→        depth += stripped.count("}") - stripped.count("{")
   361→        if depth <= 0 and re.search(r"\btry\b", stripped):
   362→            return True
   363→    return False
   364→
   365→
   366→def _check_json_parse_unguarded(
   367→    filepath: str, lines: list[str], entries: list[dict]
   368→) -> None:
   369→    """Check for JSON.parse not inside a try block."""
   370→    for line_num, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
   371→        if not _JSON_PARSE_RE.search(line):
   372→            continue
   373→        stripped = line.lstrip()
   374→        if stripped.startswith("//"):
   375→            continue
   376→        # Skip JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)) — safe deep-clone idiom
   377→        if _JSON_DEEP_CLONE_RE.search(line):
   378→            continue
   379→        if _is_in_try_scope(lines, line_num):
   380→            continue
   381→        entries.append(
   382→            _make_security_entry(
   383→                filepath,
   384→                line_num,
   385→                line,
   386→                check_id="json_parse_unguarded",
   387→                summary="JSON.parse() without try/catch — may throw on malformed input",
   388→                severity="low",
   389→                confidence="low",
   390→                remediation="Wrap JSON.parse() in a try/catch block",
   391→            )
   392→        )
   393→
   394→
   395→def _check_rls_bypass(filepath: str, content: str, lines: list[str], entries: list[dict]) -> None:
   396→    """Check for CREATE VIEW without security_invoker in SQL files."""
   397→    for m in _CREATE_VIEW_RE.finditer(content):
   398→        # Find the line number
   399→        line_num = content[: m.start()].count("\n") + 1
   400→        # Check if security_invoker is set in the view definition (next ~20 lines)
   401→        view_block = content[m.start() : m.start() + 500]
   402→        if not _SECURITY_INVOKER_RE.search(view_block):
   403→            entries.append(
   404→                _make_security_entry(
   405→                    filepath,
   406→                    line_num,
   407→                    lines[line_num - 1] if 0 < line_num <= len(lines) else "",
   408→                    check_id="rls_bypass_views",
   409→                    summary="SQL VIEW without security_invoker=true may bypass RLS",
   410→                    severity="high",
   411→                    confidence="medium",
   412→                    remediation="Add 'WITH (security_invoker = true)' to the view definition",
   413→                )
   414→            )
   415→

1→"""Python language security + coverage wiring helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import shutil
     6→
     7→from desloppify.base.discovery.source import collect_exclude_dirs
     8→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import DetectorCoverageStatus, LangSecurityResult
     9→from desloppify.languages.python.detectors.bandit_adapter import detect_with_bandit
    10→from desloppify.languages.python._helpers import scan_root_from_files
    11→
    12→
    13→def missing_bandit_coverage() -> DetectorCoverageStatus:
    14→    return DetectorCoverageStatus(
    15→        detector="security",
    16→        status="reduced",
    17→        confidence=0.6,
    18→        summary="bandit is not installed — Python-specific security checks will be skipped.",
    19→        impact=(
    20→            "Python-specific security coverage is reduced; clean security output may "
    21→            "miss shell injection, unsafe deserialization, and risky SQL/subprocess patterns."
    22→        ),
    23→        remediation="Install Bandit: pip install bandit",
    24→        tool="bandit",
    25→        reason="missing_dependency",
    26→    )
    27→
    28→
    29→def python_scan_coverage_prerequisites() -> list[DetectorCoverageStatus]:
    30→    if shutil.which("bandit") is not None:
    31→        return []
    32→    return [missing_bandit_coverage()]
    33→
    34→
    35→def detect_python_security(files, zone_map) -> LangSecurityResult:
    36→    scan_root = scan_root_from_files(files)
    37→    if scan_root is None:
    38→        return LangSecurityResult(entries=[], files_scanned=0)
    39→
    40→    exclude_dirs = collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root)
    41→    result = detect_with_bandit(scan_root, zone_map, exclude_dirs=exclude_dirs)
    42→    coverage = result.status.coverage()
    43→    return LangSecurityResult(
    44→        entries=result.entries,
    45→        files_scanned=result.files_scanned,
    46→        coverage=coverage,
    47→    )
    48→
    49→
    50→__all__ = [
    51→    "detect_python_security",
    52→    "missing_bandit_coverage",
    53→    "python_scan_coverage_prerequisites",
    54→]

    30→_BINARY_FORMATTER_RE = re.compile(
    31→    r"\bBinaryFormatter\b|\bSoapFormatter\b",
    32→    re.IGNORECASE,
    33→)

    35→
    36→def detect_csharp_security(
    37→    files: list[str],
    38→    zone_map: FileZoneMap | None,
    39→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    40→    """Detect C#-specific security issues. Returns (entries, files_scanned)."""
    41→    entries: list[dict] = []
    42→    scanned = 0
    43→
    44→    for filepath in files:
    45→        if not filepath.endswith(".cs"):
    46→            continue
    47→        if zone_map is not None:
    48→            zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
    49→            if zone in (Zone.GENERATED, Zone.VENDOR):
    50→                continue
    51→
    52→        try:
    53→            content = Path(filepath).read_text(errors="replace")
    54→        except OSError as exc:
    55→            logger.debug(
    56→                "Skipping unreadable C# file %s in security detector: %s", filepath, exc
    57→            )
    58→            continue
    59→
    60→        scanned += 1
    61→        lines = content.splitlines()
    62→        for line_num, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
    63→            stripped = line.lstrip()
    64→            if stripped.startswith("//"):
    65→                continue
    66→
    67→            if _SQL_INTERPOLATION_RE.search(line) or _SQL_CONCAT_RE.search(line):
    68→                entries.append(
    69→                    security_detector_mod.make_security_entry(
    70→                        filepath,
    71→                        line_num,
    72→                        line,
    73→                        security_detector_mod.SecurityRule(
    74→                            check_id="sql_injection",
    75→                            summary="Potential SQL injection: dynamic SQL command construction",
    76→                            severity="critical",
    77→                            confidence="high",
    78→                            remediation="Use parameterized SQL commands with SqlParameter.",
    79→                        ),
    80→                    )
    81→                )
    82→
    83→            if _RNG_IN_SECURITY_CONTEXT_RE.search(line):
    84→                entries.append(
    85→                    security_detector_mod.make_security_entry(
    86→                        filepath,
    87→                        line_num,
    88→                        line,
    89→                        security_detector_mod.SecurityRule(
    90→                            check_id="insecure_random",
    91→                            summary="Insecure random in security-sensitive context",
    92→                            severity="medium",
    93→                            confidence="medium",
    94→                            remediation="Use RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes or a cryptographic RNG.",
    95→                        ),
    96→                    )
    97→                )
    98→
    99→            if _DISABLED_TLS_VERIFY_RE.search(line):
   100→                entries.append(
   101→                    security_detector_mod.make_security_entry(
   102→                        filepath,
   103→                        line_num,
   104→                        line,
   105→                        security_detector_mod.SecurityRule(
   106→                            check_id="weak_crypto_tls",
   107→                            summary="TLS certificate validation disabled",
   108→                            severity="high",
   109→                            confidence="high",
   110→                            remediation="Remove custom callback or validate certificates properly.",
   111→                        ),
   112→                    )
   113→                )
   114→
   115→            if _BINARY_FORMATTER_RE.search(line):

   128→                    )
   129→                )

    74→        lang.complexity_map[entry["file"]] = entry["score"]

   142→def run_phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRun, *, log_fn) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:

   166→        options=orphaned_detector_mod.OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   167→            extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   168→            extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   169→            dynamic_import_finder=deps_detector_mod.find_python_dynamic_imports,
   170→        ),
   171→    )
   172→    orphan_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, orphan_entries, "orphaned")
   173→    results.extend(make_orphaned_issues(orphan_entries, log_fn))
   174→
   175→    facade_entries, _ = facade_detector_mod.detect_reexport_facades(graph)
   176→    facade_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, facade_entries, "facade")
   177→    results.extend(make_facade_issues(facade_entries, log_fn))
   178→
   179→    mixin_entries, coupling_candidates = (
   180→        coupling_contracts_detector_mod.detect_implicit_mixin_contracts(path)
   181→    )
   182→    mixin_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, mixin_entries, "coupling")
   183→    for entry in mixin_entries:
   184→        attr_preview = ", ".join(entry["required_attrs"][:4])
   185→        if len(entry["required_attrs"]) > 4:
   186→            attr_preview += f", +{len(entry['required_attrs']) - 4} more"
   187→        required_count = entry["required_count"]
   188→        tier = 4 if required_count >= 6 else 3
   189→        confidence = "high" if required_count >= 6 else "medium"
   190→        results.append(
   191→            state_mod.make_issue(
   192→                "coupling",
   193→                entry["file"],
   194→                entry["class"],
   195→                tier=tier,
   196→                confidence=confidence,
   197→                summary=(
   198→                    f"Implicit host contract: {entry['class']} depends on {required_count} "
   199→                    f"undeclared self attrs ({attr_preview})"
   200→                ),
   201→                detail={
   202→                    "subtype": "implicit_mixin_contract",
   203→                    "required_attrs": entry["required_attrs"],
   204→                    "required_count": required_count,
   205→                    "line": entry.get("line"),
   206→                },
   207→            )
   208→        )
   209→
   210→    log_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} coupling/structural issues total")
   211→    potentials = {
   212→        "single_use": adjust_potential(zone_map, single_candidates),
   213→        "cycles": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   214→        "orphaned": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   215→        "facade": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   216→        "coupling": adjust_potential(zone_map, coupling_candidates),
   217→    }
   218→    return results, potentials

    18→    """Extract all Python functions for duplicate detection."""

    20→    for filepath in find_py_files(path):
    21→        functions.extend(extract_py_functions(filepath))
    22→    return functions
    23→
    24→
    25→def scan_root_from_files(files: list[str]) -> Path | None:
    26→    """Derive the common ancestor directory from a list of file paths."""
    27→    py_files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(".py")]
    28→    if not py_files:
    29→        return None
    30→    try:
    31→        common = Path(os.path.commonpath(py_files))
    32→        return common if common.is_dir() else common.parent
    33→    except ValueError:
    34→        return None
    35→
    36→

1→"""Health score aggregation helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.base.text_utils import is_numeric
     6→from desloppify.engine._scoring.policy.core import (
     7→    MECHANICAL_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS,
     8→    MECHANICAL_WEIGHT_FRACTION,
     9→    MIN_SAMPLE,
    10→    SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS,
    11→    SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION,
    12→)
    13→
    14→
    15→def _normalize_dimension_name(name: str) -> str:
    16→    return " ".join(str(name).strip().lower().split())
    17→
    18→
    19→def _mechanical_dimension_weight(name: str) -> float:
    20→    return float(
    21→        MECHANICAL_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS.get(
    22→            _normalize_dimension_name(name),
    23→            1.0,
    24→        )
    25→    )
    26→
    27→
    28→def _subjective_dimension_weight(name: str, data: dict) -> float:
    29→    subjective_meta = (
    30→        data.get("detectors", {}).get("subjective_assessment", {})
    31→        if isinstance(data, dict)
    32→        else {}
    33→    )
    34→    configured = (
    35→        subjective_meta.get("configured_weight")
    36→        if isinstance(subjective_meta, dict)
    37→        else None
    38→    )
    39→    if is_numeric(configured):
    40→        return max(0.0, float(configured))
    41→
    42→    return float(
    43→        SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS.get(
    44→            _normalize_dimension_name(name),
    45→            1.0,
    46→        )
    47→    )
    48→
    49→
    50→def compute_health_breakdown(
    51→    dimension_scores: dict,
    52→    *,
    53→    score_key: str = "score",
    54→) -> dict[str, object]:
    55→    """Return pool averages and weighted contribution breakdown for score transparency."""
    56→    if not dimension_scores:
    57→        return {
    58→            "overall_score": 100.0,
    59→            "mechanical_fraction": 1.0,
    60→            "subjective_fraction": 0.0,
    61→            "mechanical_avg": 100.0,
    62→            "subjective_avg": None,
    63→            "entries": [],
    64→        }
    65→
    66→    mech_sum = 0.0
    67→    mech_weight = 0.0
    68→    subj_sum = 0.0
    69→    subj_weight = 0.0
    70→    mechanical_rows: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
    71→    subjective_rows: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
    72→
    73→    for name, data in dimension_scores.items():
    74→        score = float(data.get(score_key, data.get("score", 0.0)))
    75→        is_subjective = "subjective_assessment" in data.get("detectors", {})
    76→        if is_subjective:
    77→            configured = max(0.0, _subjective_dimension_weight(name, data))
    78→            effective = configured
    79→            subj_sum += score * effective
    80→            subj_weight += effective
    81→            subjective_rows.append(
    82→                {
    83→                    "name": str(name),
    84→                    "score": score,
    85→                    "configured_weight": configured,
    86→                    "effective_weight": effective,
    87→                }
    88→            )
    89→            continue
    90→
    91→        checks = float(data.get("checks", 0) or 0)
    92→        sample_factor = min(1.0, checks / MIN_SAMPLE) if checks > 0 else 0.0
    93→        configured = max(0.0, _mechanical_dimension_weight(name))
    94→        effective = configured * sample_factor
    95→        mech_sum += score * effective
    96→        mech_weight += effective
    97→        mechanical_rows.append(
    98→            {
    99→                "name": str(name),
   100→                "score": score,
   101→                "checks": checks,
   102→                "sample_factor": sample_factor,
   103→                "configured_weight": configured,
   104→                "effective_weight": effective,
   105→            }
   106→        )
   107→
   108→    mech_avg = (mech_sum / mech_weight) if mech_weight > 0 else 100.0
   109→    subj_avg = (subj_sum / subj_weight) if subj_weight > 0 else None
   110→
   111→    if subj_avg is None:
   112→        mechanical_fraction = 1.0
   113→        subjective_fraction = 0.0
   114→        overall_score = round(mech_avg, 1)
   115→    elif mech_weight == 0:
   116→        mechanical_fraction = 0.0
   117→        subjective_fraction = 1.0
   118→        overall_score = round(subj_avg, 1)
   119→    else:
   120→        mechanical_fraction = MECHANICAL_WEIGHT_FRACTION
   121→        subjective_fraction = SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION
   122→        overall_score = round(
   123→            mech_avg * mechanical_fraction + subj_avg * subjective_fraction,
   124→            1,
   125→        )
   126→
   127→    entries: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
   128→    for row in mechanical_rows:
   129→        pool_share = (
   130→            float(row["effective_weight"]) / mech_weight if mech_weight > 0 else 0.0
   131→        )
   132→        per_point = mechanical_fraction * pool_share
   133→        score = float(row["score"])
   134→        entries.append(
   135→            {
   136→                "name": str(row["name"]),
   137→                "pool": "mechanical",
   138→                "score": score,
   139→                "checks": float(row["checks"]),
   140→                "sample_factor": float(row["sample_factor"]),
   141→                "configured_weight": float(row["configured_weight"]),
   142→                "effective_weight": float(row["effective_weight"]),
   143→                "pool_share": pool_share,
   144→                "overall_per_point": per_point,
   145→                "overall_contribution": per_point * score,
   146→                "overall_drag": per_point * (100.0 - score),
   147→            }
   148→        )
   149→
   150→    for row in subjective_rows:
   151→        pool_share = (
   152→            float(row["effective_weight"]) / subj_weight if subj_weight > 0 else 0.0
   153→        )
   154→        per_point = subjective_fraction * pool_share
   155→        score = float(row["score"])
   156→        entries.append(
   157→            {
   158→                "name": str(row["name"]),
   159→                "pool": "subjective",
   160→                "score": score,
   161→                "checks": 0.0,
   162→                "sample_factor": 1.0,
   163→                "configured_weight": float(row["configured_weight"]),
   164→                "effective_weight": float(row["effective_weight"]),
   165→                "pool_share": pool_share,
   166→                "overall_per_point": per_point,
   167→                "overall_contribution": per_point * score,
   168→                "overall_drag": per_point * (100.0 - score),
   169→            }
   170→        )
   171→
   172→    return {
   173→        "overall_score": overall_score,
   174→        "mechanical_fraction": mechanical_fraction,
   175→        "subjective_fraction": subjective_fraction,
   176→        "mechanical_avg": mech_avg,
   177→        "subjective_avg": subj_avg,
   178→        "entries": entries,
   179→    }
   180→
   181→
   182→def compute_health_score(
   183→    dimension_scores: dict,
   184→    *,
   185→    score_key: str = "score",
   186→) -> float:
   187→    """Budget-weighted blend of mechanical and subjective dimension scores."""
   188→    return float(
   189→        compute_health_breakdown(dimension_scores, score_key=score_key)[
   190→            "overall_score"
   191→        ]
   192→    )
   193→
   194→
   195→__all__ = ["compute_health_breakdown", "compute_health_score"]

    24→)
    25→
    26→
    27→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    28→class ScoreBundle:
    29→    dimension_scores: dict[str, dict]
    30→    strict_dimension_scores: dict[str, dict]
    31→    verified_strict_dimension_scores: dict[str, dict]
    32→    overall_score: float
    33→    objective_score: float
    34→    strict_score: float
    35→    verified_strict_score: float
    36→
    37→
    38→def compute_dimension_scores_by_mode(
    39→    issues: dict,
    40→    potentials: dict[str, int],
    41→    *,
    42→    subjective_assessments: dict | None = None,
    43→    allowed_subjective_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
    44→) -> dict[ScoreMode, dict[str, dict]]:
    45→    """Compute dimension scores for lenient/strict/verified_strict in one pass."""
    46→    results: dict[ScoreMode, dict[str, dict]] = {mode: {} for mode in SCORING_MODES}
    47→
    48→    for dim in DIMENSIONS:
    49→        totals = {
    50→            mode: {
    51→                "checks": 0,
    52→                "failing": 0,
    53→                "weighted_failures": 0.0,
    54→                "detectors": {},
    55→            }
    56→            for mode in SCORING_MODES
    57→        }
    58→
    59→        for detector in dim.detectors:
    60→            potential = potentials.get(detector, 0)
    61→            if potential <= 0:
    62→                continue
    63→
    64→            detector_stats = detector_stats_by_mode(detector, issues, potential)
    65→            for mode in SCORING_MODES:
    66→                pass_rate, failing, weighted = detector_stats[mode]
    67→                totals[mode]["checks"] += potential
    68→                totals[mode]["failing"] += failing
    69→                totals[mode]["weighted_failures"] += weighted
    70→                totals[mode]["detectors"][detector] = {
    71→                    "potential": potential,
    72→                    "pass_rate": pass_rate,
    73→                    "failing": failing,
    74→                    "weighted_failures": weighted,
    75→                }
    76→
    77→        for mode in SCORING_MODES:
    78→            total_checks = totals[mode]["checks"]
    79→            if total_checks <= 0:
    80→                continue
    81→            dim_score = (
    82→                max(
    83→                    0.0,
    84→                    (total_checks - totals[mode]["weighted_failures"]) / total_checks,
    85→                )
    86→                * 100
    87→            )
    88→            results[mode][dim.name] = {
    89→                "score": round(dim_score, 1),
    90→                "tier": dim.tier,
    91→                "checks": total_checks,
    92→                "failing": totals[mode]["failing"],
    93→                "detectors": totals[mode]["detectors"],
    94→            }
    95→
    96→    for mode in SCORING_MODES:
    97→        append_subjective_dimensions(
    98→            results[mode],
    99→            issues,
   100→            subjective_assessments,
   101→            FAILURE_STATUSES_BY_MODE[mode],
   102→            allowed_dimensions=allowed_subjective_dimensions,
   103→        )
   104→    return results
   105→
   106→
   107→def compute_dimension_scores(
   108→    issues: dict,
   109→    potentials: dict[str, int],
   110→    *,
   111→    strict: bool = False,
   112→    subjective_assessments: dict | None = None,
   113→    allowed_subjective_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
   114→) -> dict[str, dict]:
   115→    """Compute per-dimension scores from issues and potentials."""
   116→    mode: ScoreMode = "strict" if strict else "lenient"
   117→    return compute_dimension_scores_by_mode(
   118→        issues,
   119→        potentials,
   120→        subjective_assessments=subjective_assessments,
   121→        allowed_subjective_dimensions=allowed_subjective_dimensions,
   122→    )[mode]
   123→
   124→
   125→def compute_score_bundle(
   126→    issues: dict,
   127→    potentials: dict[str, int],
   128→    *,
   129→    subjective_assessments: dict | None = None,
   130→    allowed_subjective_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
   131→) -> ScoreBundle:
   132→    """Compute all score channels from one scoring engine pass."""
   133→    by_mode = compute_dimension_scores_by_mode(
   134→        issues,
   135→        potentials,
   136→        subjective_assessments=subjective_assessments,
   137→        allowed_subjective_dimensions=allowed_subjective_dimensions,
   138→    )
   139→
   140→    lenient_scores = by_mode["lenient"]
   141→    strict_scores = by_mode["strict"]
   142→    verified_strict_scores = by_mode["verified_strict"]
   143→
   144→    mechanical_lenient_scores = {
   145→        name: data
   146→        for name, data in lenient_scores.items()
   147→        if "subjective_assessment" not in data.get("detectors", {})
   148→    }
   149→
   150→    return ScoreBundle(
   151→        dimension_scores=lenient_scores,
   152→        strict_dimension_scores=strict_scores,
   153→        verified_strict_dimension_scores=verified_strict_scores,
   154→        overall_score=compute_health_score(lenient_scores),
   155→        objective_score=compute_health_score(mechanical_lenient_scores),
   156→        strict_score=compute_health_score(strict_scores),
   157→        verified_strict_score=compute_health_score(verified_strict_scores),
   158→    )
   159→
   160→
   161→__all__ = [
   162→    "ScoreBundle",
   163→    "compute_dimension_scores_by_mode",
   164→    "compute_dimension_scores",
   165→    "compute_health_breakdown",
   166→    "compute_health_score",
   167→    "compute_score_bundle",
   168→    "compute_score_impact",
   169→    "get_dimension_for_detector",
   170→]
   171→

    58→def phase_dupes(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
    59→    """Shared phase runner: detect duplicate functions via lang.extract_functions.
    60→
    61→    When a zone map is available, filters out functions from zone-excluded files
    62→    before the O(n^2) comparison to avoid test/config/generated false positives.
    63→    """
    64→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
    65→
    66→    # Filter out functions from zone-excluded files.
    67→    if lang.zone_map is not None:
    68→        before = len(functions)
    69→        functions = [
    70→            f
    71→            for f in functions
    72→            if lang.zone_map.get(getattr(f, "file", "")) not in EXCLUDED_ZONES
    73→        ]
    74→        excluded = before - len(functions)
    75→        if excluded:
    76→            log(f"         zones: {excluded} functions excluded (non-production)")
    77→
    78→    entries, total_functions = detect_duplicates(functions)
    79→    issues = make_dupe_issues(entries, log)
    80→    return issues, {"dupes": total_functions}

   111→                    f"(window {entry['window_size']} lines): {loc_preview}"
   112→                ),
   113→                detail={

   115→                    "window_size": entry["window_size"],

   118→                },

   127→
   128→def _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(
   129→    entries: list[dict[str, Any]], zone_map
   130→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   131→    """Keep only in-scope, zone-allowed boilerplate clusters.
   132→
   133→    jscpd can return files that are outside language discovery (artifacts/docs).
   134→    Restricting to known zone-map files prevents unknown paths from being treated
   135→    as production issues.
   136→    """
   137→    if zone_map is None:
   138→        return entries
   139→
   140→    known_files = set(zone_map.all_files())
   141→    filtered: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   142→    skipped = 0
   143→    for entry in entries:
   144→        locations = entry.get("locations", [])
   145→        kept_locations = [
   146→            loc
   147→            for loc in locations
   148→            if loc.get("file") in known_files
   149→            and not should_skip_issue(
   150→                zone_map,
   151→                loc.get("file", ""),
   152→                "boilerplate_duplication",
   153→            )
   154→        ]
   155→        distinct_files = {loc["file"] for loc in kept_locations}
   156→        if len(distinct_files) < 2:
   157→            skipped += 1
   158→            continue
   159→
   160→        normalized = dict(entry)
   161→        normalized["locations"] = sorted(
   162→            kept_locations,
   163→            key=lambda item: (item.get("file", ""), item.get("line", 0)),
   164→        )
   165→        normalized["distinct_files"] = len(distinct_files)
   166→        filtered.append(normalized)
   167→
   168→    if skipped:
   169→        log(f"         zones: {skipped} boilerplate clusters excluded")
   170→    return filtered
   171→

   173→def find_external_test_files(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> set[str]:
   174→    """Find test files in standard locations outside the scanned path."""
   175→    extra = set()
   176→    path_root = path.resolve()
   177→    project_root = get_project_root()
   178→    test_dirs = lang.external_test_dirs or ["tests", "test"]
   179→    exts = tuple(lang.test_file_extensions or lang.extensions)
   180→    for test_dir in test_dirs:
   181→        d = project_root / test_dir
   182→        if not d.is_dir():
   183→            continue
   184→        if d.resolve().is_relative_to(path_root):
   185→            continue  # test_dir is inside scanned path, zone_map already has it
   186→        for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
   187→            for filename in files:
   188→                if any(filename.endswith(ext) for ext in exts):
   189→                    extra.add(os.path.join(root, filename))
   190→    return extra
   191→

   201→    """Convert detector entries to normalized issues."""
   202→    results: list[Issue] = []
   203→    for entry in entries:

   229→def _coverage_to_dict(coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus) -> dict[str, Any]:
   230→    return {
   231→        "detector": coverage.detector,
   232→        "status": coverage.status,
   233→        "confidence": round(coerce_confidence(coverage.confidence), 2),
   234→        "summary": coverage.summary,
   235→        "impact": coverage.impact,

   237→        "tool": coverage.tool,

   241→
   242→def _merge_detector_coverage(
   243→    existing: dict[str, Any],
   244→    incoming: dict[str, Any],
   245→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   246→    merged = dict(existing)
   247→    merged["status"] = (
   248→        "reduced"
   249→        if str(existing.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   250→        or str(incoming.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   251→        else "full"
   252→    )
   253→    merged["confidence"] = round(
   254→        min(
   255→            coerce_confidence(existing.get("confidence")),
   256→            coerce_confidence(incoming.get("confidence")),
   257→        ),
   258→        2,
   259→    )
   260→
   261→    for key in ("summary", "impact", "remediation", "tool", "reason"):
   262→        current = str(merged.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   263→        update = str(incoming.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   264→        if update and not current:
   265→            merged[key] = update
   266→        elif update and current and update not in current:
   267→            merged[key] = f"{current} | {update}"
   268→    return merged

   271→def _record_detector_coverage(lang: LangRuntimeContract, coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus | None) -> None:
   272→    if coverage is None:

   275→    detector = str(normalized.get("detector", "")).strip()
   276→    if not detector:
   277→        return
   278→    existing = lang.detector_coverage.get(detector)
   279→    if isinstance(existing, dict):
   280→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = _merge_detector_coverage(existing, normalized)
   281→    else:
   282→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = normalized

   390→        per_file_cache = {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if k not in _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS}
   391→        review_cache = {"files": per_file_cache}

   422→def phase_signature(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   423→    """Shared phase runner: detect signature variance via lang.extract_functions.
   424→
   425→    Backend-agnostic — works with any extractor that returns FunctionInfo objects
   426→    (tree-sitter, regex, AST, etc.).  Returns empty results when the lang has no
   427→    function extractor.
   428→    """
   429→    from desloppify.engine.detectors.signature import detect_signature_variance
   430→
   431→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
   432→
   433→    issues: list[Issue] = []
   434→    potentials: dict[str, int] = {}
   435→
   436→    if not functions:
   437→        return issues, potentials
   438→
   439→    entries, _total = detect_signature_variance(functions, min_occurrences=3)
   440→    for e in entries:
   441→        issues.append(make_issue(
   442→            "signature", e["files"][0],
   443→            f"signature_variance::{e['name']}",
   444→            tier=3, confidence="medium",
   445→            summary=(
   446→                f"'{e['name']}' has {e['signature_count']} different signatures "
   447→                f"across {e['file_count']} files"
   448→            ),
   449→        ))
   450→    if entries:
   451→        potentials["signature"] = len(entries)
   452→        log(f"         signature variance: {len(entries)}")
   453→
   454→    return issues, potentials
